Repeated-subject time-course evidence. The Issue 212 repeated-subject example experiment uses
the rna layer to assess the declared condition target contrasts treatment with control. Thin
lines connect repeated observations from each subject; Bold lines show stored population
trajectories from the rank-scale model with subject-specific random intercepts and time slopes;
Red crosses mark recorded early endpoints. The analysis unit is complete subject trajectory;
the design is longitudinal; the estimand is condition-by-time interaction on the rank scale;
time is recorded as day; subjects are identified by mouse_id; adjustment uses batch. Facet
labels report stored interaction intervals and resampling recurrence. Raw p-values are
retained; q-values use Holm correction across declared components within each metadata field
and evidence variant. 2 subject endpoints are marked as ending before the final observed study
time. No acceptance threshold is applied. Trajectory evidence is exploratory and does not
establish biological validity.
